questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable, with room for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Don't panic. Release the accelerator and slow down. Keep both hands on the wheel and steer gently back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop at these red eight-sided signs.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic signal means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, regardless of traffic signals.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm is extended upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: When turning left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start from the left lane when turning left on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop serious bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two one-way roads with a median between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when facing an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially around children. Look directly at the area behind your car.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply to the right first, then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
Slow down and sound their horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is watching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They show drivers road conditions and help them drive safely. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns of hazards ahead or nearby.
Tells drivers a school zone is ahead.
Tells drivers a recreation area is ahead.
Tells drivers where to find food and gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of hazards ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards ahead or nearby. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for cars on the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. You must let vehicles and pedestrians in or entering the intersection pass first. Go only when it is safe.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only:

options.text: To prevent a problem with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a problem with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles pass when they use a siren or air horn and have flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions they give over their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only go when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: You have had an upsetting incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let out your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar for a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let others pass, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have lost control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a problem that could make it unsafe. You should:

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that could affect your vehicle's safe operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.
